entityDescription:
New monitoring technologies are being progressively implemented in coastal ocean observatories. These new observing systems, such as IMOS, OOI, IOOS, VENUS, POSEIDON, COSYNA among others, are delivering new insight into coastal ocean variability, that triggers new theoretical and technological developments, increasing our understanding of open ocean, coastal and nearshore processes and contributing to a more science based and sustainable management of the oceans and coastal areas.
SOCIB is one of such systems, a Coastal Ocean Observing and Forecasting System located in the Balearic Islands, a new facility of facilities open to international access. SOCIB responds to a change of paradigm in the observation of our oceans and coasts, an observation that has evolved from being centered on a unique platform, the oceanographic ships with data availability being delayed in time, to an observation now based on multi-platform and integrated systems (using buoys, satellites, ships, autonomous underwater vehicles, HF radar, ARGO profilers, etc.), also assuring quasi real time quality controlled data availability for both researchers and society. This change of paradigm is very significant and allows being able to respond to the three key drivers identified by SOCIB back in 2009: (1) science priorities, (2) technology development, (3) response capacity to society needs.
SOCIB is a multi-platform distributed and integrated system that provides streams of oceanographic data and modelling services to support operational oceanography in a European and international framework, therefore also contributing to the needs of marine and coastal research in a global change context. In line with EuroGOOS, operational oceanography is here understood in a wide sense, including both the systematic long-term measurements of the seas and their interpretation and dissemination, and also the sustained supply of multidisciplinary data to cover the needs of a wide range of scientific research and societal priorities. This allows a quantitative increase in our understanding of key questions on oceans and climate change, coastal ocean processes, ecosystem variability, sea level rise, etc. and also drives us towards a more science based coastal and ocean management. It is important to note that in its present format and financial status, SOCIB isl not be carrying out direct research activities (except in specific areas directly related to SOCIB objectives) but provides support for them. The research activities are being carried out by IMEDEA, COB/IEO and UIB, among other organisations, in close coordination to SOCIB.

entityDescription:
Created in 2002, by the Autonomous Region of Aosta Valley, Fondazione Montagna sicura (Safe Mountain Foundation) is a non-profit foundation with its headquarter located in Courmayeur (AO), at the foot of the Mont-Blanc massif. Fondazione Montagna sicura is a centre for applied research, training and documentation focused on innovative applications of new technologies to mountain territories. The Foundation is active on several projects, pursuing various objectives, such as the promotion of mountain safety through research and dissemination activities, the analysis of hydro-geological risks, the promotion of sustainable development through pilot tests and best practices, and the study of climate change impacts on high-altitude environments and the cryosphere. Core activity of Fondazione Montagna sicura is the glacier-related risk-monitoring plan. Based on an annually updated GIS database of Aosta Valley’s glaciers, derived from historical data and several years of field research and observations, this monitoring plan aim to identify and investigate existing or potentially new risk situations across the territories of the Autonomous Region of Aosta Valley. The research and monitoring activities conducted on the dynamics of Planpincieux Glacier (Courmayeur - AO), as well as the
risk management actions undertaken for the potential GLOF (Glacial Lake Outburst Flood) of the Gran Croux Glacier (Cogne - AO), and the monitoring of rockfall-induced risk of the Brenva basin (Courmayeur - AO) are only the latest of several activities operated thanks to this plan. This knowledge become therefore a key tool for the numerous cross-border cooperation projects that, since its establishment, the Foundation has been committed to develop, together with universities (University of Turin, Polytechnic of Turin, University of Genova, .), research centers (WLS, ARPA, CREALP, CNR IRPI, EURAC, BFW, Geoformer, ETH Zurich, Geopraevent, IGE Grenoble etc.), and public administrations, aiming for a broad sharing of experiences and effective impacts on the territories affected by these issues.

entityDescription:
Climate change is a defining issue of our time, and we are at a critical moment of irreversible damage to our planet. From changing weather patterns that threaten food production to rising sea levels that increase the risk of catastrophic floods, the impacts of climate change are global in scope and on an unprecedented scale. Without stronger action today to mitigate global warming, it will be more difficult and expensive to adapt to its inevitable future impacts.
City air is a sorry state. It is dirty and hot. Outdoor pollution kills 4.2 million people a year, according to World Health Organization and the problem is likely to get worse. Now, 55% of the people live in cities and 2050 that share is expected to reach 68%, so far cities are responsible for 70% of global greenhouse gas emissions. Greenhouse gas “GHG” emission is a serious problem and has negative impacts on the urban quality life, population´s health (large amounts of public spending related to health and well-being derived from pollutants), agriculture and water. City governments are important agents of action due to their close relationships with local businesses and citizens. All key collaborators together must take increasingly strict measures of prevention and solve these problems. Currently, there is not so much understanding and transparency of the real impact of Greenhouse emission from natural and human activities due to a lack of appropriate system and methodologies that help governments and institutions to identify assess, track, and provide accurate diagnostics of air, and therefore, provide the most appropriate corrective measurements. 
Under this context, Dynamic Genesis offer an innovative monitoring system of measurement, that relies on unique algorithm named AxSat that process data from Copernicus Sentinel 5P and identify average of CH4, NO2, SO2, O3 concentration and provides information about Greenhouse gas emission to urban domain to the society in general, through a methodology that consist of monitoring (AxSat maps), Report (AxSat analytics), Verification (AxSat GHG Inventory) and Implementation (decarbonization strategies and some come cases Carbon market strategies). Benefits of our product and service are:
a) Estimate of the amount and type of GHG emission to obtain more transparent, accurate and comparable reporting of air quality diagnostics, that mean develop more cost and time effective strategies of reduction and mitigation of carbon.
b) Support subnational government entities such as cities and states that represent large GHG source regions e.g. megacities with actionable information on their GHG emission to evaluate and guide progress towards emissions reduction goals.
c) Provide Information to industry and private sectors businesses that will help locate and quantify previously unknown emission reduction opportunities.
d) Provide information to GHG inventory builders in support of their efforts to reduce uncertainty of national inventory report to UNFCCC.
e) Support the Paris Agreement global stock take as government and UNFCCC.
